# Lane D fixtures

Generated by lane D; each subdirectory names its generating script and pinned time.

## `pki/`

The Certomancer test PKI that pyHanko's signing tests use
(`data/pyhanko/crypto/certomancer.yml`), exported with
`crates/hanko-sign/oracle/export_pki.py` (pyHanko 0.38.1, Certomancer 0.16.0):

```sh
python -I crates/hanko-sign/oracle/export_pki.py \
    crates/hanko-testdata/data/pyhanko/crypto crates/hanko-testdata/data/lanes/d/pki
```

One directory per architecture with DER certificates (`<label>.crt`) and a
`manifest.json` (issuer, subject key, revocation, services). Private keys are
not copied: the manifest names the key file under `data/pyhanko/crypto/`
(pyHanko's public test keys) and its passphrase.

Certificate validity periods are fixed by the configuration, so the export
does not depend on the time it runs. RSA and Ed25519 signatures are
deterministic; ECDSA and DSA certificate signatures use a random nonce, so a
re-export yields different but equivalent certificates for those
architectures. `testing-ca-dsa/signer1-sha512` is skipped (asn1crypto cannot
encode `sha512_dsa`; pyHanko's tests never use it).

License: MIT (derived from pyHanko test data, see `data/pyhanko/LICENSE-pyHanko`).

## `revinfo/`

OCSP responses and CRLs that Certomancer's live services (pyHanko's
`pki_services` fixture) return at the times pyHanko's signing tests freeze
the clock to, exported with `crates/hanko-sign/oracle/export_revinfo.py`:

```sh
python -I crates/hanko-sign/oracle/export_revinfo.py \
    crates/hanko-testdata/data/pyhanko/crypto crates/hanko-testdata/data/lanes/d/revinfo
```

Layout: `<arch>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/ocsp-<cert label>.der` (no nonce) and
`crl-<repo label>.der`. The Rust tests serve them through fake OCSP / CRL
fetchers (`tests/support/services.rs`). RSA signatures are deterministic.
